Alex —

Thanks for flagging this and for sending the artifacts. I’m sorry your PM had that experience. I’ve looped in Monica (People Ops) and Marissa (their manager) to start an internal intake. We’ll treat this as confidential — please do not share the PM’s name outside your team; we want to limit exposure while we triage.

- If needed, we’ll arrange a temporary reassignment or remove the engineer from the Thursday session pending the intake.
- I’ll follow up here with a proposed interim plan within 24 hours.

If your PM is willing, a short written note (even a sentence) would help the intake. If not, we will proceed based on the artifacts you provided.

Appreciate the discretion.

Best,

Subject: Re: Concern about conduct during last onsite — intake questions + confidentiality reminder

Team —

I reviewed the timeline and the Slack screenshot. A few quick items to support the intake:
- Can Alex confirm whether the Slack screenshot was in a public channel or DM?
- Has the PM asked us to take any tangible actions (reassignment, no-contact, mediation)?
- Is there a specific deliverable on Thursday that would be impacted by a reassignment?

Important: please remember this is a confidential intake. Per policy, avoid discussing the employee’s name over broad channels (no All-company messages, no Slack threads except a private HR channel). I’ve copied Lauren from legal for confidentiality/retaliation guidance.

I’ll start a private intake file (HR-1123) and will pull any historical notes. For now I recommend we pause the Thursday session until we confirm next steps; it’s a low-cost mitigant and protects the PM.

Attachments: meeting-notes-20260811.pdf (summary of intake conversation with Alex)

Thanks — Monica

Jonas, if you approve, I’ll send the private notice and update the calendar. Monica, please confirm if you want to interview the PM before we finalize the reassignment.
